study: Ager/Styles/Sizmur/Worth 2015 (NFER eval), Oxford Improving Numeracy and Literacy Programme, EEF
eval_evidence: EEF-funded efficacy RCT independently evaluated by NFER (its own Code of Practice, separate ethical review); the programme was developed/delivered by a separate University of Oxford team.
developer_evidence: The University of Oxford team (programme developers) delivered the one day of training and the implementation support visit, and provided ongoing technical support 'as and when required' (p.6, p.13).
cascade_evidence: Class teachers attended a day of training delivered by the Oxford research/developer team and received a support visit from an Oxford team member; no train-the-trainer/lead-teacher intermediary.
counterfactual_evidence: Shared control group received 'no training and continued to teach literacy and numeracy in the way they would normally' (true BAU); report flags only a risk of contamination, not an active alternative.
coaching_evidence: Beyond one day of training, support was one implementation visit plus ongoing technical support provided 'as and when required'; no recurring in-class coaching cycles.
student_dose_evidence: Programme lessons (replacing ~1hr/week) included a pupil-facing online computer-games/activities component; greater game use was associated with greater numeracy impact (p.7, pp.40-41) — a substantial student-facing software dose.
maturity_evidence: Single 10-12 week programme delivered once to Year 2 pupils within one school year; no recurring annual rollout / no prior implementation-year maturity axis.
